what_it_measured.text: Aim: This retrospective study explored a panel of NITs for assessing response to semaglutide treatment in patients with MASH randomised in a phase 2b trial (NCT02970942).

3.3 | Baseline NIT Characteristics of Patients With Change in ≥ 1 Fibrosis Stage (Progression or Improvement) We evaluated baseline levels of NITs in patients with ≥ 1 stage of fibrosis progression (n = 15) or improvement (n = 25) in the placebo group (prognostic context of use).

dose.text: In total, 320 patients were randomised and treated for 72 weeks with semaglutide 0.1 mg (80 patients), 0.2 mg (78 patients), or 0.4 mg (82 patients), or placebo (80 patients).
3 | Results 3.1 | Baseline NIT Characteristics Of the 268 participants in the completer population, 202 received semaglutide (72, 62 and 68 received 0.1, 0.2 and 0.4 mg,

endpoint.text: More patients had MASH improvement and fewer had fibrosis progression versus placebo when assessed by a 20% NIT response (0.5 U for ELF); among patients with baseline LSM > 8 kPa and ELF > 9.8 U, a larger proportion achieved LSM < 8 kPa and ELF < 9.8 kPa with semaglutide versus placebo.
Treatment response was evaluated by NITs using either mean changes, responder groups, or risk categories from baseline to week 72.

Multiple NITs (alanine transaminase, aspartate transaminase [AST], controlled attenuation parameter, CK18-M30/M65, SomaSignal nonalcoholic steatohepatitis tests, FibroScan-AST, NIS-4, metabolomics advanced steatohepatitis fibrosis score, fibrosis-4 index, liver stiffness measure [LSM], enhanced liver fibrosis [ELF], PRO-C3 and ADAPT) were assessed.

reported_results.text: More patients had MASH improvement and fewer had fibrosis progression versus placebo when assessed by a 20% NIT response (0.5 U for ELF); among patients with baseline LSM > 8 kPa and ELF > 9.8 U, a larger proportion achieved LSM < 8 kPa and ELF < 9.8 kPa with semaglutide versus placebo.
Note: Bold text denotes statistically significant results (p < 0.05).
The accuracy of FIB- 4 in classifying future fibrosis progression was 75.0% (AUC 0.69, sensitivity 53.3%, specificity 81.1%) (Table S3).
Best differentiation was observed with SS-f ibrosis (mean score for improvement 0.48 vs. 0.70 for non-improvement; p = 0.00040).
Note: Bold text denotes statistically significant results (p < 0.05).
